To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

conditional visuo-goal associations, rather than visuomotor associations, are the fundamental mechanism underlying goal-directed behavior and that the PMd and the dlPFC play a major role in determining the salience of goals, whereas the PMd, the dlPFC, the vlPFC, and the BG contribute to specifying the actions to achieve the goal.

the PMd and the dlPFC play major roles in maintaining goal salience, whereas the vlPFC plays a major role in representing the visual signals and in determining goals based on the signals, and that the BG play a restrictive role in specifying action.
the PMd, dlPFC, vlPFC, and BG are involved in goal-directed behavior mediated conditional visuo-goal associations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying goal-directed behavior.
the neural mechanisms underlying conditional visuo-goal associations, which are thought to be involved in the control of goal-directed behavior.
the identification of the neural substrates and mechanisms underlying goal-directed behavior mediated through the conditional visuo-goal framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the four areas contribute to goal-directed action mediated by conditional visuomoto association in the following manner: The PMd is involved in maintaining salience of the visual signals, whereas the dlPFC is involved in maintaining the saliency of the goals; the vlPFC contributes to the identification of the visual signals and the goals and the BG is involved in selecting actions.
conditional visuo-goal associations are mediated by a cortico-BG network that involves PMd, dlPFC, and vlPFC.
the four areas are involved differently in goal-directed behavior mediated either by conditional visuomotion association or by conditional visuo-object association.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
conditional visuo-goal signals are represented by the four areas in an area-dependent way.
conditional visuomotors and visuo-goals are represented in the cortical and subcortical areas, respectively, and that these two representations are integrated in the BG.
conditional visuomotors association is a more general process than conditional visuo-goal, and that the former is a subset of the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PMd, dlPFC, vlPFC, and BG contribute to goal-directed action mediated by conditional visu-goal association.
the four areas play different roles in the process of goal-directed behavior, depending on whether they are involved in conditional visuo-goal or conditional visuomotion association.
the cortical-basal ganglia circuits involved in conditional visuo-goal associations are more flexible and general than those involved in conditional visuospatial associations.
